description: Release-age cooldown is inherited, not configured here: config:best-practices extends security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm, which sets minimumReleaseAge=3 days + internalChecksFilter=strict for the npm datasource.

DO NOT restate minimumReleaseAge on a packageRule that matches lockFileMaintenance or pin. That preset deliberately sets it to null for those update types because Renovate cannot age them; a rule here sorts AFTER the preset and would override the carve-out. With minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour=timestamp-required (default since Renovate 42) a missing timestamp counts as not-yet-passed, so the branch is never created — silently stopping the daily lockFileMaintenance run that is this repo's only transitive-dep refresh path (ADR-0027 § 2026-08-06 amendment).

The npm-side cooldown for those paths lives in .npmrc (min-release-age=3). Non-npm datasources — docker, github-tags, github-release-attachments, git-refs — carry NO cooldown; see ADR-0027 § 2026-08-28 amendment for why that is a documented non-goal rather than an oversight.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Daily, and exempt from the global PR limits. This is the ONLY Renovate mechanism that refreshes transitive npm deps — vulnerability PRs cover direct deps only (https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/#osvvulnerabilityalerts). On the weekly window behind prConcurrentLimit=1 it was starved for 9 weeks while transitive advisories sat open; the per-branch limit calc (calcLimit in lib/workers/global/limits.ts) treats 0 as 'no limit', same exemption vulnerabilityAlerts uses.

packageRules.description: MinIO RELEASE.* tags sort lexicographically — use loose versioning so timestamp order is respected

Caddy version appears in three places in docker/caddy/Dockerfile (FROM caddy:X-builder, FROM caddy:X, xcaddy build vX), all tracked against the `caddy` Docker image — the two FROM tags via the built-in dockerfile manager, the xcaddy build version via the customManager below. Group them so one PR advances all three to the same version together; sharing one datasource is what makes that lockstep hold. The caddy-dns/cloudflare plugin SHA tracks separately (git-refs).

Suppress abandonment-heuristic false positives — release-date heuristic misfires on stable / maintenance-mode libs. Per-dep rationale + per-row verification dates in docs/ops/dep-management.md § Abandonment-flag verdicts. 3 years keeps real abandonment within range while filtering current noise.

Auto-merge all non-major updates (patch, minor, digest, pin, lockfile maintenance) on green CI — grouped clusters included; grouping consolidates PRs, it does not gate the merge (requires repo Settings → General → Pull Requests → Allow auto-merge)

Belt-and-braces: never auto-merge major bumps. The rule above opts in only non-major types, so majors already fall through to no auto-merge — this states the exclusion explicitly and survives edits to the rule above

customManagers.description: Caddy version inside `xcaddy build vN.N.N` in docker/caddy/Dockerfile. Tracks the `caddy` Docker image (not github-releases) so the built version can only advance to a Caddy release that already has a published image — keeping it in lockstep with the FROM caddy:X base tags, which the dockerfile manager bumps from the same datasource. Grouped under groupName 'caddy' above.
caddy-dns/cloudflare plugin pinned to a git SHA — track master and bump the SHA
MinIO `mc` image tag in sync-*.sh helper scripts — track minio/mc Docker tags with loose versioning

MinIO `minio` and `mc` images hardcoded in `docker run …` shell inside .github/workflows/<name>.yml and .github/actions/<name>/<file>.{yml,sh} (one directory level only — a nested action dir would silently drop out of tracking) — Renovate's github-actions manager doesn't parse docker images inside run: blocks or sibling scripts, so a custom regex keeps them in lockstep with the docker-compose copies

PostgreSQL major in Alpine apk pins (`postgresqlN`, `postgresqlN-client`, `postgresqlN-contrib`) inside Dockerfile.backup. Renovate's Docker manager bumps the `db` image tag in docker-compose/CI but does not see apk package names. Without this regex a server bump leaves the backup client major behind — pg_dump/pg_restore older→newer is the unsupported direction. extractVersion filters Docker tags to integer-only so we track the major line, matching what the apk package name encodes.

CLI binaries installed by download URL + SHA256 verification (OSV-Scanner, actionlint, ripgrep, age), in a workflow step or a composite-action step — `age` lives in `.github/actions/install-age/install-age.sh`, called from both `ci.yml`'s `check-shard` and `e2e.yml`, so the pattern list covers `.github/actions/<name>/*.{yml,yaml,sh}`. Both halves are load-bearing: a composite's procedure belongs in a sibling `.sh` so CI's shellcheck gate covers it (actionlint does not read `action.yml`), which is where `install-age`'s and `start-minio`'s pins sit, and `action.yml` stays in scope because a composite may still hold an inline `run:` block. Keep the pattern list and the scan roots in `scripts/check-renovate-annotations.mjs` in step: the check scans that same file set, so a class it scans but no manager covers is reported as an untracked pin. None fits the github-actions manager — the first two ship only a Docker action or a reusable workflow, the latter two ship no action at all — so without this manager each is a pin with no update path, the failure mode ADR-0027 exists to retire. The github-release-attachments datasource locates the release's checksums asset from the current digest and re-reads it on the next release, so version and SHA256 advance in the SAME PR — a hand-edited checksum is never required. When no checksums asset matches (age ships only Sigsum `.proof` files) it falls back to hashing the release assets directly and matching on the digest, so a checksum-less upstream is still tracked. Driven by an inline `# renovate:` annotation so the dep is declared at the call site rather than inferred from a URL shape. TWO constraints, both silent when violated: (1) `currentValue` MUST be the literal git tag, `v` prefix and all or neither — `v2.3.8` for OSV-Scanner, `15.2.0` for ripgrep, because the digest lookup calls `GET /releases/tags/{currentValue}` verbatim and either an added or a stripped `v` 404s there. Steps must therefore reference the version through the `version` variable exactly once, deriving any unprefixed form (`${version#v}`) — Renovate rewrites the matched span only. (2) The annotation, `version=` and `expected_sha=` must be CONSECUTIVE lines: matchStrings joins them with `\s+`, so an interposed comment drops the pin out of tracking with no error raised anywhere. `scripts/check-renovate-annotations.mjs` is the guard against both.
